Question B-003-003-002.

Why the correct answer is right: At very-high-frequency (VHF), the radio-frequency (RF) amplifier must add very little noise because noise introduced at the first receive stage degrades weak signals before later gain.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Product detector": A product detector recovers audio from single-sideband (SSB) or continuous-wave (CW) signals. Low-noise design is most critical at the RF input stage.
- sourceIndex 2: "IF amplifier": The intermediate-frequency (IF) amplifier matters, but noise added after front-end gain is less damaging than noise added before the signal is established.
- sourceIndex 3: "Limiter": The limiter removes amplitude variation in frequency modulation (FM). It is not the VHF low-noise front-end stage.
